evidence.paraphrase: The page describes a broad weekly measure intended to capture U.S. financial conditions across money, debt, equity, and traditional and shadow-banking systems.
One hundred five financial variables are standardized and combined into an index whose historical mean is zero and standard deviation is one.
Risk, credit, and leverage subindexes expose the source of movements, while the adjusted NFCI removes variation associated with current activity and inflation.
Positive values mean tighter conditions relative to the historical average, not a structural neutral rate or an automatically causal estimate of future growth effects.

executive_summary: The Chicago Fed NFCI summarizes 105 weekly financial indicators as a standardized broad conditions index and exposes risk, credit, and leverage subindexes. Its adjusted version removes variation associated with contemporaneous activity and inflation, while positive readings mean tighter-than-average conditions. MacroTrace should keep the raw and adjusted objects separate and expose loading, coverage, normalization, and macro-adjustment diagnostics.
